DeploymentShape: one central inference service; model replicated per worker
ModelResidency: whole model loaded on every active worker
Routing: no family routing after request enters inference service
FailureScope: worker failure; model-level issue affects all triage handled by that version
Versioning: single model artefact/version plus service version
OperationalImplication: Simple routing and version coordination, but every worker carries the full model and every model release has estate-wide blast radius.

DeploymentShape: one central inference service; all family models resident in each worker
ModelResidency: all family models loaded on every worker
Routing: select one or more candidate families inside inference service
CrossModelCoordination: required when evidence or pathway membership spans family boundaries
FailureScope: worker failure; individual family artefact defect can be isolated logically
OperationalImplication: Keeps deployment simple while preserving smaller inference units, but memory may approach the aggregate size of all family models and duplicate shared features.

DeploymentShape: one central inference service with model cache; families loaded on demand
ModelResidency: hot families cached; cold families loaded from artefact store
Routing: family routing occurs before model acquisition
CrossModelCoordination: fan-out may load or query several family models for ambiguous cases
ScalingUnit: inference worker plus family-model cache capacity
FailureScope: cache/load failure may affect a family or request; service can remain available
Versioning: immutable family artefacts referenced by manifest
OperationalImplication: Can reduce resident memory, but introduces cold-load latency, cache policy, artefact availability and more observable runtime states.

DeploymentShape: central inference service with shared/common model layer plus family models
ModelResidency: shared layer resident; family models resident or cached according to policy
Routing: shared evidence evaluated first or alongside family routing; one or more families then engaged
CrossModelCoordination: explicit contract between shared layer and family models
ScalingUnit: shared-layer worker capacity plus family inference capacity
FailureScope: shared-layer defect has broad blast radius; family defect can remain localised
Versioning: shared-core version plus compatible family versions in a release manifest
OperationalImplication: Reduces uncontrolled duplication of common evidence, but creates the most explicit compatibility and coordination requirements.
